answer.justification: Hoarseness after thyroidectomy indicates vocal cord paralysis from recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. This nerve runs in the tracheoesophageal groove closely related to branches of the inferior thyroid artery near the lower pole, so ligation here risks injuring it. Internal laryngeal nerve injury is sensory (aspiration risk), external laryngeal nerve injury causes loss of high pitch rather than hoarseness, and edema is not persistent at 2 weeks.
